what_it_does: Spiking neural networks are a brain-inspired style of AI where neurons fire brief binary pulses (spikes) instead of continuous numbers, which can be very energy efficient but is hard to accelerate when combined with the attention mechanism (the part of modern AI that decides which pieces of information to focus on). Bishop is an accelerator for this combination. It groups spikes from many tokens (pieces of input) and time steps into bundles, then routes dense bundles to a hardware array optimized for dense computation and sparse bundles to a separate hardware array optimized for sparse computation — matching the hardware to the data rather than forcing one size to fit all. Special training techniques encourage the network to produce sparser bundles, and a pruning method with a mathematical error guarantee removes low-value spikes before attention is computed.
